name: Silverbough Hart
cultural_role: significant respected hunt animal; natural death antlers used ceremonially
description: A major old-wild browsing cervid feeding on mid-canopy foliage, antlerthorn, veilvine, and tender shoots. The Silverbough Hart is hunted by the elves — respected but not sacred — with hunt rarer than Feywoodhorn Stag due to lower population. Antlers from naturally-shed or naturally-died individuals are used for ceremonial items.

name: Silverbough White Hart
cultural_role: sacred; never hunted or pursued; appearances absent for generations
description: An extremely rare all-white variant of the Silverbough Hart lineage. Deep old-wild only. A sacred sighting; never hunted or pursued. Appearances may be absent for generations. The White Hart is a significant omen in the Feywood's cultural tradition.

name: Feywoodhorn Stag
cultural_role: primary elven hunt animal; proving-hunt quarry
description: The more numerous major cervid of the Feywood. Feywoodhorn are grazer-browsers feeding on whispergrass, low-canopy foliage, and antlerthorn. Primary elven hunt animal — respected but not sacred — and the canonical proving-hunt quarry.

name: Rootback Elk
cultural_role: rarely hunted; cross-palette species with Temperate Forest range
description: A heavy browser of wetter old-growth margins, basin-edge clearings, and Heartwater Basin outskirts. Rarely hunted by elves. Cross-palette species — canonically present in the Temperate Forest as well as the Feywood via cross-Border range.

name: Briarmane Courser
cultural_role: prestige elven mount; prized bond animal; Feywood's signature courser
description: A tall, lean courser of the Feywood — named for the dark thorn-and-silver pattern running down its mane and tail. Briarmanes are admired for their speed and the ambient-field-sensitivity they share with other Feywood-touched creatures. Occasional hunt quarry when unbonded; canonically companion-capable. See `briarmane_courser` in `data/companions/creatures.json` for the companion profile.

name: Hearthgoat
cultural_role: semi-domesticated dairy animal; household-scale husbandry; personal family bonds
description: A semi-domesticated / semi-wild dairy bovid kept at household scale across the Feywood. Hearthgoats provide milk and cheese; their husbandry is low-intensity and family-scale. Household hearthgoats form genuine personal attachments to keeping families across generations.

name: Moonthorn Wolf
cultural_role: Feywood's defining canid; exceptional elven life-bonds (Ash)
description: The principal Feywood pack predator and the defining canid of the outer wild. Colloquially "Feywood wolves." Moonthorn packs hunt Feywoodhorn stag, rootback elk, boar of the briar, and briarmane courser; they take silverbough hart rarely. In exceptional circumstances a moonthorn wolf may form a deep life-bond with an individual elf — the relationship is pack, not domestication. House Heartwood has had bonded moonthorn wolves across generations (Ash is Sylvara's bonded wolf). See `moonthorn_wolf` in `data/companions/creatures.json` for the companion profile.

name: Mossveil Cat
cultural_role: emblem of quiet danger, patience, unseen movement
description: A solitary ambush predator of the denser Outer Old-Growth Wild, estate-border forest, and shadowed understory. Mossveils take Feywoodhorn stag, smaller deer, foxes, and briarmane courser young. They are the Feywood's emblem of quiet danger, patience, and unseen movement.

name: Oldroot Bear
cultural_role: respected old-forest strength; not lightly hunted
description: A major omnivore of berry zones, nut groves, fungal grounds, and riparian margins. Oldroots primarily eat plant mass and fish; they take Feywoodhorn stag calves and injured animals opportunistically. Respected old-forest strength; not lightly hunted. Seasonal visits to the Heartwater Basin during fish runs are canonical.

name: Hollowcrown Owl
cultural_role: reads ambient field; appears at disturbance edges before disturbances are visible
description: A mythic-rare deep-wild owl — the rare apex nocturnal bird predator of the Feywood. Hollowcrown owls read the Feywood's ambient field and appear at disturbance edges before disturbances are visible. Occasional sightings beyond the Feywood are reported; elves treat realm-side Hollowcrown sightings as significant omens regardless of distance.

name: Thornroot Stalker
cultural_role: deep-wild danger; field-illegible in its direction
description: A rare deep-wild apex predator with a distinctive ambient-field property: field-illegible. Sensitive visitors notice the Feywood's ambient character becoming suddenly less readable in the stalker's direction. Thornroots take silverbough hart, Feywoodhorn stag, rootback elk, rare moonthorn wolves, and opportunistically humans and elves. Rare, deep-wild-only, genuinely dangerous.

name: Duskpetal Fox
cultural_role: bridge species between inhabited and wild spaces; common in folklore
description: A small predator/omnivore of the Thornveil margins, Vaelmere edge, estate surrounds, and outer wild. Duskpetal foxes are a bridge species between inhabited and wild spaces; they feature prominently in Feywood folklore. A small but genuine companion candidate for handlers with patience.

name: Silverback Marten
description: A mid-size mustelid of Heartwater Basin margins and Outer Old-Growth Wild. Silverbacks are agile and secretive; they forage aquatic and arboreal prey alike.

name: Winterweasel
cultural_role: canonical seasonal indicator (coat whitens in late Turning)
description: A small mustelid whose coat whitens in late Turning. The Winterweasel is a canonical seasonal indicator; druids and long-tenured elves watch its coat change as a marker of the Feywood's seasonal state.

name: Boar of the Briar
cultural_role: elven hunt quarry; less symbolically weighty than Feywoodhorn
description: An omnivorous boar of the deeper wild. A Feywood hunt quarry secondary to Feywoodhorn Stag in symbolic weight; boar meat is a more practical elven protein source than ceremonial occasion.

name: Feywood Hare
description: A widespread browse-opportunist across the Feywood's lighter zones. Common prey for duskpetal fox, mossfoot hound, and the Feywood's smaller raptors.

name: Canopy Squirrel
cultural_role: nut and seed dispersal, especially around Hearthnut
description: A small arboreal rodent critical to Hearthnut and oak mast dispersal. Canopy squirrels are abundant around Thornveil's Hearthnut groves and through the mature Outer Wild canopy.

name: Thornquill
description: A small spiny understory mammal of the deeper wild. Thornquills forage quietly; their spines deter most predators short of the apex tier.

name: Dormouse
description: A small understory rodent, common prey across the Feywood. Ubiquitous in cluster gardens, cultivated plots, and the broader forest understory.

name: Shrewsong
cultural_role: beloved of elven children; dusk-whistle call is a domestic-garden soundmark
description: A small insectivore named for its distinctive high whistling call at dusk. Shrewsongs are beloved of elven children; their call is one of the ambient sounds of Thornveil cluster gardens during warm seasons.

name: Mistwing Hawk
cultural_role: messenger symbolism; widespread day raptor
description: A day raptor widespread across the Feywood. Mistwings carry canonical messenger symbolism in Feywood tradition and are prized by rangers as scouts and message birds. See `mistwing_hawk` in `data/companions/creatures.json` for the companion profile.

name: Thornsong Owl
cultural_role: omen bird; watchfulness
description: A small-to-medium woodland owl associated with watchfulness in Feywood tradition. Thornsong calls carry an omen quality in cultural register without rising to Hollowcrown significance.

name: Boughowl
cultural_role: cross-palette species; Temperate Forest range
description: A larger woodland owl of the deeper Feywood forests. Cross-palette species — canonically shared with the Temperate Forest palette and present in the Feywood via cross-Border range.

name: Cranemoor Heron
cultural_role: waterline sentinel; departure is a Turning indicator
description: A large heron-analog wading the Heartwater Basin margins. Cranemoors are canonical waterline sentinels; early departure from the Basin is a Turning indicator druids watch for.

name: Silverstream Trout
cultural_role: primary elven protein source; health-indicator via population density
description: The primary Heartwater Basin fish and a standard elven protein source. Silverstream population health is a Turning indicator; thinning populations in the shallows register before broader decline visible above water.

name: Lakepike
cultural_role: apex freshwater predator; specific individuals remembered across generations
description: The apex fish of the Heartwater Basin's lake. Large, ambush-feeding, rare but known. Older elven fishers speak of specific lakepike holding specific water for generations.

name: Feywood Otter
cultural_role: common along Basin shallows; family groups; handled gently by elves
description: Common along Heartwater Basin shallows and reed-margins. Feywood otters live in small family groups and are handled gently by the elves who share their water. A companion candidate for handlers with sustained relationship to Basin work.

name: Heartpond Frog
cultural_role: chorus species; primary health-indicator monitored by druids
description: An amphibian chorus species whose evening chorus is ambient canonical sound of the Heartwater Basin margins. The Heartpond frog chorus is among the Feywood's primary health-indicator signals; silence in warm-season evenings where chorus should be is a significant druidic alert.

name: Stardrift Beetle
cultural_role: bioluminescent firefly; brightness correlates with Heartwood health
description: A bioluminescent insect — the canonical firefly of the Feywood. Stardrift brightness and abundance correlate with Heartwood health; emergences diminish under Turning and cease under Stillfall. Their seasonal spectacle is one of the Feywood's named natural events.

name: Honeybound Bee
cultural_role: primary Feywood pollinator; honey and wax production; honey mead base
description: The Feywood's primary pollinator, producing distinctive Feywood honey — a minor trade good and the key ingredient in honey mead. Honeybound hives are wild; elves tend them loosely but do not domesticate. Honeybound health is a separately trackable register among the Feywood's health indicators.

name: Soilkeeper Beetle
description: The primary decomposer beetle in Feywood leaf litter. Soilkeepers maintain the detrital cycle supporting Rootlace Mycelium's nutrient exchange role.

name: Briar-Stinger
cultural_role: warm-season evening nuisance near Basin margins
description: A biting-insect nuisance active in warm-season evenings near Heartwater Basin margins. Briar-stingers are localized; Basin residents know to accommodate and the broader Feywood is not affected.

name: Mossfoot Hound
cultural_role: pack canid below moonthorn wolf in territory
description: A pack-forming smaller canid of the outer wild — a mid-tier apex in its territory, below moonthorn wolf range. Mossfoots are more approachable than moonthorns and serve as companion candidates for Feywood handlers who cannot or do not seek the deeper exceptional bond moonthorns represent.

name: Greymantle Crow
cultural_role: the Feywood's observers; watching a person intently is a cultural signal
description: The Feywood's corvid, glossy dark grey in coloring. Intelligent and commonly seen around noble estates and Thornveil's outskirts. Greymantles are the Feywood's observers; elven tradition holds that a greymantle watching a person intently warrants reflection. A companion candidate for patient handlers; the bond is cognitive rather than obedient.
